audit_findings.title: Deferred contract investment may be omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.933m FY2026 cash-flow deduction, equal to 25.1% of the $190.7m anchor; the roll-forward shows $48.338m of net capitalized costs above amortization
audit_findings.mechanism: The net investment in deferred commissions and implementation costs reduces current owner earnings and therefore the OE anchor used throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: These capitalized costs are amortized over the expected period of benefit, which the Company increased from 7 years to 8 years effective June 30, 2026, on a prospective basis, based on the Company’s average client life and growth of term contract renewals beyond their initial terms.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial current-period reinvestment, but the supplied valuation does not show whether it was retained in the $190.7m anchor. If omitted, the error is large enough to change the valuation materially; the possibility is unresolved rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor line by line to FY2026 cash flow and the deferred-contract-cost roll-forward; if the $47.933m outflow was excluded or added back, restore it and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Client-fund interest appears to have been stripped despite being operating float income
audit_findings.magnitude: $119.964m FY2026 pretax revenue, equal to 62.9% of the $190.7m anchor; normalized after-tax OE impact is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing client-fund interest lowers operating OE even though the client-fund assets generating it are excluded from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest income earned on funds held for clients is recognized in Interest income on funds held for clients when earned as the collection, holding and remittance of these funds are components of providing services to clients.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies this interest as revenue arising from client-service activities. The valuation method says portfolio interest was purged but does not disclose whether the purge included the $119.964m client-fund stream. If it did, value is materially understated; the appropriate normalized amount must reflect taxes, credit risk, liquidity costs and sustainable rates.
audit_findings.action: Separate corporate-cash interest from client-fund interest in the OE reconciliation, normalize the latter using sustainable balances and yields net of associated costs and taxes, and rerun the valuation with that amount retained in OE.

audit_findings.title: All corporate cash may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified required-cash portion of the filed $271.917m balance; the full balance equals $4.81 per share and 9.2% of $2,951m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating or collateral cash should be excluded from the excess-cash equity bridge rather than added dollar for dollar to common-equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Depending on the magnitude of such an event, we may be required to seek additional sources of short-term liquidity, which may not be available on reasonable terms, if at all, and our operating results and our liquidity could be adversely affected and our banking relationships could be harmed.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates settlement liquidity exposure but does not quantify minimum operating cash, collateral requirements or probable funding needs. Consequently, the record cannot determine how much of the $271.917m bridge addition is unavailable to owners or whether the adjustment is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain bank and ACH collateral terms, peak settlement exposures, historical reversals or defaults, management's minimum cash policy and available committed liquidity; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized SBC may escape the no-add-back rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.817m FY2026, equal to 6.2% of anchor OE; if treated as a continuing anchor correction, the base operating PV would fall by approximately $166.0m or $2.94 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized SBC is an economic compensation cost that neither reduced FY2026 earnings nor appears in the $69.302m cash payment for capitalized software; it must enter OE as reinvestment or an equivalent compensation charge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company capitalized $ 14,376 , $ 12,996 and $ 11,817 of stock-based compensation expense in its capitalized internal-use software costs in the years ended June 30, 2024, 2025 and 2026, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $11.817m capitalized amount, but the supplied valuation lacks enough reconciliation detail to prove whether an equivalent charge was made. If the model deducted only cash software spending and income-statement SBC, the anchor is overstated by an amount capable of materially affecting value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile total FY2026 software additions of $81.773m to the $69.302m cash outflow and $11.817m capitalized SBC; if no equivalent charge exists, deduct the capitalized SBC from OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may rely on acquisitions whose cash cost is excluded
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified future acquisition requirement; filed acquisition cash payments were $277.851m in FY2025 and $49.183m in FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth is overstated if projected OE expansion requires recurring acquisition spending that is not deducted as reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: However, we expect to fund our operations, capital expenditures, acquisitions, share repurchases and other investments principally with cash flows from operations, and to the extent that our liquidity needs exceed our cash from operations, we would look to our cash on hand or utilize the remaining borrowing capacity under our credit facility to satisfy those needs.
audit_findings.explanation: Airbase and Grayscale contribute to the current earnings perimeter, but excluding their historical purchase prices from recurring OE is not itself an error. The open issue is forward-looking: the record does not establish whether the 0%, 3% and 6% growth paths require additional acquisitions, while organic client count grew 7% in FY2026.
audit_findings.action: Track organic revenue, OE and client growth separately from acquired contributions; rerun growth scenarios with recurring acquisition spending only if evidence shows that forecast growth cannot be achieved organically.

audit_findings.title: The lease context omits signed but uncommenced payments
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.563m undiscounted over 10.6 years, averaging approximately $0.808m annually or 0.42% of the $190.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Future occupancy expense could reduce forecast OE after the lease commences; the commitment also supplements lease-liability context.
audit_findings.evidence: The table above excludes $ 8,563 of undiscounted future minimum lease payments for operating lease liabilities for office space that had not yet commenced for a term of 10.6 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is real, but its simple annual scale is less than one-half of one percent of anchor OE, and $8.563m is only 0.29% of base equity value even before discounting. It is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the commencement date and resulting annual expense is included in projected operating costs; rerun only if the actual annual charge materially exceeds the filed commitment's implied scale.
